Sender

STATIC DISPLAY

Creating a matrix automatically stages its sender manifest on the recording server. Keep the matrix unchanged through all four phases. The receiver upload finalizes the pair; then create the next matrix.

Collection code · shared automaticallyCreate a matrix first

Optical grid-size markers, repeated phase cues and grid-8 references. Rectified crops use 4×4 pixels per cell. Create a matrix; the receiver discovers its collection code, expected grid and split automatically.

Each new sequence has fresh random bytes. Keep one session for the same device arrangement; start a new session after changing devices or returning later. All phases of a payload stay in the same training split.

02

Receiver

AUTOMATIC SESSION

The receiver gets the collection code, expected grid and split from the recording server, then reads the grid-size markers from the camera image and checks they agree. Keep that one matrix displayed through all four phases. No sender pixels, random seed or labels enter acquisition.

The assignment locks while a batch contains recordings. Upload and clear the batch before switching matrices. On a static server, enter the code and expected grid manually. The optical size must match; a wrong grid is never assigned to this batch.

Distance compares aligned, color-corrected captures of the same phase. We aim for a mostly similar pool with some variation, not the largest possible distance. Severe blur, wrong phase or wrong geometry should not count as useful diversity.

Start the camera; alignment checks run automatically.

Uploads contain calibrated pixels, device/browser/camera metadata and optional original PNGs. Recording stays local until you press Upload. Downloads remain available. Each batch contains one grid size; upload or download it before clearing. The physical session and split remain fixed across batches. The selected 200 / 400 / 800 MiB budget covers all four phases, up to 128 samples. G16–G64 fit 32 per phase at 200 MiB. G128 fits 8 per phase at 200 MiB, 16 at 400 MiB or 32 at 800 MiB. Choose the larger budget before recording. Browser memory use is higher than the encoded file size.
